paragraphs.text: No. The filing representative cannot attest for the applicant or owner and cannot submit the job filing. The applicant must complete the Applicant of Record’s Attestation and electronic signature before the application can be submitted; the applicant also uploads the required DPL-1, dated no more than one year before submission. The owner must complete the Owner’s Attestation to confirm authorization for the applicant to submit and acknowledgment that the application information was reviewed.

The owner should log in using the same email address entered for the owner in the Stakeholders section, review the filing, attest in the Statements & Signatures tab, and save. Filing representatives may enter and view filing information and use Preview to File to identify items still needed, but the guidance says they cannot submit filings or permits. Once the applicant and owner have completed their own required attestations, submission remains an action for the applicant.

issues.detail: The statement that submission remains an action for the applicant is not established for the job filing; the cited guidance says only that a filing representative cannot submit filings or permits, while the work-permit passage specifically identifies the permit applicant as the submitter.

The answer omits the conditional February 2026 exception that, when the Owner Type is Condo Unit Owner or Co-Op Tenant-Shareholder, a Board representative must also attest and both the owner and Board representative must complete attestations before the filing can proceed.

paragraphs.text: The plumbing scope should be filed as a subsequent filing under the existing job number—not as a new unrelated job number—if it is part of the same construction project and property. DOB NOW guidance says all filings for the same construction project should use the same job number, with an alphabetic/numeric extension identifying the filing type and sequence; a subsequent filing adds new scope of work and new work types under that job number.

A subsequent filing may use a different applicant from the initial GC filing and may have a different review type. Once submitted, it functions as a separate application, may be permitted before the initial filing is permitted, and ordinarily requires its own LOC request. For NB or Alteration-CO filings, however, the supplied specialized FAQ says an LOC is not requested for the subsequent filing; its status remains Permit Entire while the initial filing is the one that changes to CO issued.

The initial GC filing must first be submitted rather than remain in pre-filing status. The subsequent filing can then be initiated through the initial (I1) filing’s Filing Action by selecting “Subsequent Filing.” The FAQ states it may be submitted after I1 submission and until an LOC has issued for I1. The guidance also says not to place filings with the same job number in the Related DOB NOW/BIS Job Numbers field, and says subsequent filings are preferred to adding related job numbers for this purpose.
